display_name: Credit points under Income Tax Ordinance ss 33A, 34, 36 and 36A: the credit point and allowance point, two points for an Israeli resident individual, a quarter point travel credit, and half a point for a woman

language.note: English identifiers (@lang en); the Hebrew of every provision is quoted in inert strings and comments, rendered mechanically from the deposited source by render_source.py, which also checks every quotation (`python3 -I render_source.py --check *.l4`).

scope: Encoded: s 33A (the definitions of 'נקודת זיכוי' -- NIS 504 per tax year, indexed, set off against that year's tax -- and of 'נקודת קיצבה' -- the 31 December 1996 credit point as adjusted under s 120B, divided by twelve), s 34 (two points for an individual who was an Israeli resident in the tax year), s 36 (a quarter point 'as a travel credit' for an Israeli resident individual), s 36A (half a point for a woman), and the aggregate 'credit points under ss 34 and 36' that s 134A(2) names. Taken as inputs, with no default: the year's indexed credit-point value (s 120B, row IL-03), the tax it is set off against (s 121 etc., row IL-03), and Israeli residence for the tax year (s 1, not encoded). Reached and refused: s 48 (order of 5755-1995 for Area residents who are not Israeli citizens) and s 48A (Regulations of 5775-2014 for foreign workers), wherever either could decide the answer. Not encoded: ss 35, 37-48A and the rest of Part C Chapter Three (row IL-08 and others), s 66 (row IL-02), ss 120B, 121, 121B (row IL-03). Published Israel Tax Authority figures (NIS 2,904 per point for 2025; NIS 242 per point per month for 2024-2026) are carried in a separate module, labelled as published figures and not as law. Law stated as the Wikisource consolidation retrieved 2026-10-06. (0.2.0) Also encoded: s 3A(f), an Israeli citizen who is a resident of, or operates in, the Area treated 'as if' an Israeli resident, its two limbs input facts of the record `Taxpayer in a tax year`. The year-free rules over a Person take no tax year and answer every year on the deposited text (0.1.0's 'since 5764' understated this); the year-aware rules over a `Taxpayer in a tax year` refuse a year before each section's last listed amendment (s 34 1976, s 36 1978, s 36A 1997, s 33A 2005, s 3A(f) 2017) and apply the s 48A refusal from tax year 2002, s 48A's enactment, only (assumed, not ruled; forks F12, F13). (0.3.0) Forks F1, F2 and F4 are switches in the year-aware rules, by default declining where the text does not decide (Meng's ruling SHRUG of 2026-10-08).

years_answered.year-free rules (over a Person): every tax year, on the deposited text; s 48A refused in every year; s 3A(f) not seen
years_answered.year-aware rules (over a Taxpayer in a t: s 34 from 1976, s 36 from 1978, s 36A from 1997, s 33A (every amount in NIS) from 2005, the s 3A(f) route from 2017; each from the first tax year beginning after the Hebrew year of the section's last listed amendment ended (fork F12, assumed, not ruled); a year after 2026 is a projection of the text at retrieval
years_answered.s 48A: refused from tax year 2002, s 48A having been enacted in 5763 (תשס״ג־3); before 2002 the section's own answer (fork F13: the lead's choice, assumed, not ruled, made on the repairer's objection to dating it by the Regulations of 5775-2014)
years_answered.s 48: not dated: refused wherever the section's text governs and the order could decide

forks.F1: s 36A has no residence limb (unlike ss 34 and 36), and s 48 does not list it: read literally, a non-resident woman gets half a point. (0.3.0) RULED by Meng 2026-10-08 (SHRUG): a switch, default declined where residence decides (a woman who does not count as an Israeli resident); readings 'no residence condition' and 'only to an Israeli resident' kept by name. The year-free rules keep reading A and say so. Shared with row IL-02.
forks.F2: s 36's heading speaks of travel to the place of earning; its body imposes no condition of earning or travel: the body is followed, every resident individual gets the quarter point. (0.3.0) RULED by Meng 2026-10-08 (SHRUG): a switch on a new input (income from personal exertion), default declined for an individual without such income whom s 36 would otherwise give anything; readings 'every resident individual' and 'only with income from personal exertion' kept by name. The year-free rules keep reading A and say so.
forks.F3: s 36 says 'יחיד תושב ישראל' without 'in the tax year': read as the same residence-for-the-tax-year as s 34.
forks.F4: Part-year residence: residence is one status per tax year, supplied by the caller; no apportionment by this row. (0.3.0) RULED by Meng 2026-10-08 (SHRUG): a switch on a new input (residence for the whole year, or for so many months), default declined for a part-year resident wherever a year of residence would give anything; readings 'one residence status for the whole tax year' and 'apportioned by the months of residence, as section 41 apportions' kept by name; ss 34 and 36 only. The year-free rules keep reading (i) and say so.
forks.F5: 'המקוזז כנגד המס לאותה שנה': the credit reduces that year's tax to no less than zero; no refund, no carry-over (supported by s 91's 'יתרת נקודות הזיכוי'). (0.3.0) Under SHRUG, not a switch (class b): only reading A is arguable for the tax after the set-off; whether an unused balance is paid out is not a question this row answers, and the order of credits does not arise in a rule that sets one amount against one tax.
forks.F6: s 33A indexes 'as stated in s 120A', whose definition of 'מדד' is deleted; s 120B is read as governing. No answer turns on it, because the indexed value is an input.
forks.F7: Wikisource editorial figures are not law and are not used as values.
forks.F8: The points are 'taken into account' with no claim or proof: an entitlement computed from facts, not a deontic permission.
forks.F9: 'אשה' is undefined: an input fact. (0.3.0) Under SHRUG, not a switch (class c): an input convention.
forks.F10: Where s 48 or s 48A could decide the case the model refuses, rather than answering as if the instrument did not exist or from an editor's summary of it. (0.2.0) Still so in the year-free rules; the year-aware rules date the s 48A refusal from tax year 2002, its enactment (F13). The s 48 refusal stays undated.
forks.F11: (0.2.0) s 3A(f) applies 'the provisions of this Ordinance' to an Israeli citizen (s 3A(a) sense) who is a resident of, or operates in, the Area 'as if he were an Israeli resident': read as reaching ss 34 and 36, both limbs (taken: A). Facts calling the taxpayer both an Israeli citizen in the Area and an Area resident who is not one are refused by name.
forks.F12: (0.2.0) The deposited text of a section governs a tax year that begins after the Hebrew year of its last listed amendment has ended (the lead's choice, assumed, not ruled): refuses a year an amendment may already have governed rather than answer one it may not have reached; wrong only if a Law deferred its commencement past the next 1 January.
forks.F13: (0.2.0) s 48A can take a credit away from tax year 2002, the first year its enactment in 5763 (תשס״ג־3) could reach; before 2002 the section's own answer. The lead's choice (2026-10-08, assumed, not ruled), made on the repairer's objection to the first choice, 2014 by the Regulations of 5775-2014: the note at line 1812 that records them is not law and does not exclude an earlier instrument. The refusal keeps its 0.1.0 wording, which row IL-02 copies.
